newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv to set up Russia seat belt plant.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv to set up Russia seat belt plant.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. car safety equipment company Autoliv Inc. said on Thursday it would set up a seat belt plant in Dubna, north of Moscow.
"The new plant will have an annual production capacity of one million seat belts," Autoliv said in a statement.
At the beginning of the year Autoliv started delivering seat belts made in Sweden to Russian car manufacturer Auto Vaz.
Currently deliveries correspond to an annual rate of 350,000 seat belts. The rate is expected to double next year, the company said, adding that this production would be transferred to Russia.
"After a sharp fall in car production at the beginning of the 1990s, Russian car production has stabilised and a sharp increase is expected in the next few years," Autoliv said.
"Autoliv is currently negotiating new contracts both with Auto Vaz and other Russian car manufacturers."
